newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Three hurt as bus fired on in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Three hurt as bus fired on in Bosnia.

text.p: Two children and a policeman were hurt when a local bus was fired on in Serb-controlled northern Bosnia, United Nations officials said on Wednesday.
The attack took place on Tuesday evening near the Serb-held town of Ugljevik, according to Patrik Svensson, spokesman for the U.N. International Police Task Force in Bosnia.
"The bus was fired at and two children, one girl and one boy, were injured as well as a local policeman," Svensson told a news conference.
The children were taken to hospital in the Serb town of Bijeljina but were later allowed to go home. Svensson did not know the condition of the police officer, who he assumed was a Bosnian Serb.
The attack occurred during a time of rising tension in northern Bosnia, as Moslems resettle homes in Serb areas they were forced to leave during 43 months of war.
Moslems say Serbs are blowing up houses they are trying to rebuild and Serbs accuse Moslems of illegally bringing arms into the demilitarised Zone of Separation along the wartime front line.
Although reports of explosions and armed confrontations have increased in the area lately, shootings have been rare since the fighting stopped.
U.N. police would investigate the shooting further, Svensson said.
"Of course it's very, very serious if a local bus is being fired at and we had two children injured," He said. "It's definitely serious."
U.N. officials reported that two more homes in a deserted Moslem village in northern Bosnia had been destroyed on Tuesday, but they could not give details.
